coveTube.reason: 2026-10-10 coordinator ruling (b) on the user send-back: Meshy merged the coil laps, so the uncoiled tail shows holes and fins however the contact is cut (chains 1-3); the tail past the waist is rebuilt as a swept tube along the coveTailPath centreline, welded at the waist plane and textured from the old tail's scales. numpy dry-run (tube/dry.py, linear bone blend): Move tail edges >2x 156 -> 64, max 41 -> 12, p99 1.91 -> 1.86. Chain 2: tail.segments 12 -> 24: the rest coil turns up to ~150 deg between adjacent bones at 12 segments, so the Move uncoil bends single joints ~150-170 deg and linear blend skinning flattens the swept tube there (ring min/max 0.10, chain 1 boards); 24 segments halve the per-joint bend. waistBlend 1.2 keeps the 12-segment waist blend length (0.6 x 2). The weld loop's bisect near-duplicates are welded (weldMergeFrac) and the ring angles even out over blendRings (chain 1 carried the loop's uneven angles down the tube: sub-mm tip edges, a 0.0003 weld sliver the Death heap tore 35x -> 52x). Segment-unit knobs doubled with the count so their physical reach is unchanged: tail.waistBlend 0.6 -> 1.2, tail.fuseCut (build default 1.2) -> 2.4, coveTailPath.fuseCut 1.5 -> 3.0 (at 1.5 the 24-segment cut opened holes across the waist and the weld plane had no closed loop). tail.snapGrounded 0.002 rad (build_unit opt-in): at 24 segments the Idle hips ride left ~1e-5 rad jitter on the resting coil, the glTF exporter flattened Tail_19's channel and verify_glb missed 1.2e-4 at the tip (gate 1e-4); grounded bones within 0.002 rad of rest are now exactly at rest. Chain 3 (coordinator-approved): the tube is triangulated; bake_cs welds Blender's polygons and the patch lane the GLB triangles, so quads failed the numpy CS parity gate (p99 0.013 of the height) and the Death heap could not be applied.
